conversation.user: I want to apply to Construction Management Bachelor of Technology.
conversation.advisor:
You can apply to **Construction Management – Bachelor of Technology**, a degree-completion program offered by the **School of Construction and the Environment**.

- **Campus:** Burnaby  
- **Delivery:** In person  
- **Study options:** Full-time or part-time  
- **Program focus:** Construction-project management, technical skills, and interpersonal skills  

### Admission requirements

All applicants require:

- An approved departmental **pre-entry assessment**
- **English Studies 12 with at least 73%**, or an equivalent
- **Exactly one** of the following entry pathways:

1. **Construction-related diploma or degree:** minimum 67% GPA plus at least 1 year of construction-industry work experience  
2. **Unrelated diploma or degree:** minimum 67% GPA, a **Construction Operations Associate Certificate** with at least 67% GPA, and at least 1 year of construction-industry work experience  
3. **Unrelated diploma or degree:** minimum 67% GPA plus at least 8 years of North American construction-management experience in mid- or senior-level roles  
4. **Approved Red Seal trade**, an accepted math option at 60%, a **Construction Operations Associate Certificate** with at least 67% GPA, and at least 1 year of construction-industry experience in addition to apprenticeship hours  

If your qualifying post-secondary credential was completed outside Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia, or New Zealand, an accepted comprehensive course-by-course credential evaluation with GPA calculation is required. A master’s degree alone is not sufficient for admission.

The program’s stored information does not verify application deadlines, application procedures, or document-submission timing. Review the program page for current application information:  
[Construction Management – Bachelor of Technology](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/construction-management-bachelor-of-technology-full-time-part-time-8800btech/)

conversation.user: I completed a Civil Engineering diploma. Does that qualify me?
conversation.advisor:
A **Civil Engineering diploma may qualify as the construction-related credential** for **Construction Management – Bachelor of Technology**, but the diploma alone is not sufficient.

For the construction-related credential pathway, you must also have:

- A minimum **67% GPA** from a recognized institution
- At least **1 year of construction-industry work experience**
- **English Studies 12 at 73% or equivalent**
- An approved departmental **pre-entry assessment**

If the diploma was completed outside Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia, or New Zealand, an accepted comprehensive course-by-course credential evaluation with GPA calculation is also required.

Based on what you told me, the diploma itself is the requirement that may be met; your GPA, work experience, English requirement, and assessment status are still unknown. Confirm whether the department classifies your specific Civil Engineering diploma as construction-related.

[Program information and current application details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/construction-management-bachelor-of-technology-full-time-part-time-8800btech/)

conversation.user: What else would I need for admission?
conversation.advisor:
For **Construction Management – Bachelor of Technology**, assuming your Civil Engineering diploma is accepted as a construction-related credential, you would still need:

- **At least 67% GPA** in the diploma from a recognized institution
- **At least 1 year of construction-industry work experience**
- **English Studies 12 with at least 73%**, or an equivalent
- An **approved departmental pre-entry assessment**
- Exactly one applicable admission pathway—the construction-related diploma pathway would be the relevant one if your diploma is classified that way

If your diploma was completed outside **Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia, or New Zealand**, you would also need an accepted comprehensive, course-by-course credential evaluation with GPA calculation.

Your completed **LIBS 7001 — Critical Reading and Writing** is part of the curriculum’s Liberal Studies component; it is not listed as an admission requirement.

The available information does not verify application deadlines, procedures, or document-submission timing. Review the [program information and current application details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/construction-management-bachelor-of-technology-full-time-part-time-8800btech/) and confirm with the department whether your specific Civil Engineering diploma is classified as construction-related.

For more information, see BCIT Admissions: https://www.bcit.ca/admission/.

response.answer:
For **Construction Management – Bachelor of Technology**, assuming your Civil Engineering diploma is accepted as a construction-related credential, you would still need:

- **At least 67% GPA** in the diploma from a recognized institution
- **At least 1 year of construction-industry work experience**
- **English Studies 12 with at least 73%**, or an equivalent
- An **approved departmental pre-entry assessment**
- Exactly one applicable admission pathway—the construction-related diploma pathway would be the relevant one if your diploma is classified that way

If your diploma was completed outside **Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia, or New Zealand**, you would also need an accepted comprehensive, course-by-course credential evaluation with GPA calculation.

Your completed **LIBS 7001 — Critical Reading and Writing** is part of the curriculum’s Liberal Studies component; it is not listed as an admission requirement.

The available information does not verify application deadlines, procedures, or document-submission timing. Review the [program information and current application details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/construction-management-bachelor-of-technology-full-time-part-time-8800btech/) and confirm with the department whether your specific Civil Engineering diploma is classified as construction-related.

For more information, see BCIT Admissions: https://www.bcit.ca/admission/.
